problem: Which value of $x$ satisfies the equation $\frac{1}{x}=\frac{2+x}{2x}+\frac{3}{4x}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Solving Rational Equations Containing Three Distinct Linear Denominators
examples.worked_solution:
First, note that $x = 0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

Now, let's multiply both sides of the equation by the least common denominator. The equation has the denominators $x, 6x,$ and $3x,$ so the the least common multiple (or $\textrm{LCM}$) of the denominators is

$$
\textrm{LCM}(x, 6x, 3x) = 6x.
$$

Multiplying both sides of the equation by $6x$ and simplifying, we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{1+x}{x}+\frac{5+x}{6x} & =\frac{1-x}{3x} \\ 6x\cdot (\frac{1+x}{x}+\frac{5+x}{6x}) & =6x\cdot \frac{1-x}{3x} \\ 6x\cdot (\frac{1+x}{x})+6x\cdot (\frac{5+x}{6x}) & =6x\cdot (\frac{1-x}{3x}) \\ 6x\cdot (\frac{1+x}{x})+6x\cdot (\frac{5+x}{6x}) & =2\cdot 3x\cdot (\frac{1-x}{3x}) \\ 6\cancel{x}\cdot (\frac{1+x}{\cancel{x}})+\cancel{6x}\cdot (\frac{5+x}{\cancel{6x}}) & =2\cdot \cancel{3x}\cdot (\frac{1-x}{\cancel{3x}}) \\ 6(1+x)+(5+x) & =2(1-x).\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $x,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}6(1+x)+(5+x) & =2(1-x) \\ 6+6x+5+x & =2-2x \\ 7x+11 & =2-2x \\ 7x+2x & =2-11 \\ 9x & =-9 \\ x & =-1\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, recall that we cannot allow $x=0$ as a solution. Since $x=-1$ is different from $x=0,$ we can accept it as the solution.

Therefore, the solution is $x=-1.$

We note that $d=0$ cannot be a solution since division by $0$ is undefined. 

The equation has the denominators $3d$ and $4d.$ So first, we find the least common multiple (or $\text{LCM}$) of the denominators. We find that

$$
\text{LCM}(3d,4d)=12d.
$$

So, we multiply both sides of the equation by $12d,$ and simplify: 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{10-d}{3d}+\frac{3d-5}{4d} & =1 \\ 12d(\frac{10-d}{3d}+\frac{3d-5}{4d}) & =12d\cdot 1 \\ 12d\cdot \frac{10-d}{3d}+12d\cdot \frac{3d-5}{4d} & =12d \\ 4\cdot 3d\cdot \frac{10-d}{3d}+3\cdot 4d\cdot \frac{3d-5}{4d} & =12d \\ 4\cdot \cancel{3d}\cdot \frac{10-d}{\cancel{3d}}+3\cdot \cancel{4d}\cdot \frac{3d-5}{\cancel{4d}} & =12d \\ 4(10-d)+3(3d-5) & =12d\end{aligned}
$$

We now have a linear equation in $d,$ and we can solve this using the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}4(10-d)+3(3d-5) & =12d \\ 40-4d+9d-15 & =12d \\ 25+5d & =12d \\ -7d & =-25 \\ d & =\frac{25}{7}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we recall that we cannot allow $d=0$ as a solution. However, since $d=\frac{25}{7}\ne 0,$ we conclude that the solution is $d=\frac{25}{7}.$
